responseText: {"title":"Open Mouths, Held Breath","question":"Is a face showing its teeth smiling, shouting, or something the image refuses to name?","introduction":"Twenty-five faces, each with teeth showing. Some wear flat saturated grounds that push them forward; others dissolve into scribble or shadow. None of them settle. This exhibition follows the tooth-filled mouth from its most readable forms toward works where the surrounding marks pull so hard against the opening that the expression becomes genuinely undecidable.","closing":"Each face here shows its teeth. Whether that is a greeting, a warning, or something with no name depends on marks the works themselves leave unresolved.","chapters":[{"title":"The Mouth as Readable Sign","introduction":"Four faces where the open mouth and its surroundings still allow a legible first reading — alarm, a grin, a cry — before complications set in.","stops":[{"slot":"W005","whyHere":"Looping lines and two saturated orange marks at the open mouth read as a gasp or cry, the clearest emotional signal in the gallery.","transitionFromPrevious":null},{"slot":"W045","whyHere":"Yellow-green ground and raw open mouth share W005's forward pressure, but dense lash lines and layered skin tones add a held, watchful quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"Both faces push toward the viewer on vivid grounds; W045 replaces loose loops with dense layered flesh tones, making the open mouth feel more bodily."},{"slot":"W108","whyHere":"Teeth bared and eyes fixed forward, held inside a single white boundary line against plain brown silence — the most direct confrontational address so far.","transitionFromPrevious":"W045's face dissolves at the hair edges; W108 is sharply bounded by a white outline, making the same forward pressure feel contained and deliberate."},{"slot":"W132","whyHere":"The wide-open mouth dominates the lower half while concentric framing bands press the head toward the viewer, but the closed eyes above refuse to confirm the sound below.","transitionFromPrevious":"W108's eyes are fixed and open; W132's are shut under dense crosshatching, so the open mouth below loses its confirming witness."}]},{"title":"Flat Grounds, Mask Faces","introduction":"Six works where a saturated, unmodulated background eliminates spatial retreat, turning the face into something closer to a sign or emblem than a portrait.","stops":[{"slot":"W007","whyHere":"Flat red-orange field, rectangular eye sockets, and bared teeth with smeared cheek strokes hold the face between mask-like fixity and agitation.","transitionFromPrevious":"W132's concentric bands frame a recognisable head; W007's flat red-orange ground removes all depth, pushing the face into emblem territory."},{"slot":"W012","whyHere":"Yellow ground, blank oval eyes, and a hard red crossbar divide the face into horizontal zones — mask-like stillness against restless looping surface lines.","transitionFromPrevious":"W007's red field is warm and advancing; W012 switches to yellow with a dark head, reversing the figure-ground relationship while keeping the same flat spatial logic."},{"slot":"W015","whyHere":"Two full rows of teeth, crossed and striped eyes, and dense colored lines covering every surface make this the most overtly mask-like face in the chapter.","transitionFromPrevious":"W012's face has one tooth row and some open ground; W015 doubles the teeth and fills every surface with line, intensifying the mask quality."},{"slot":"W021","whyHere":"Flower-burst eyes and hot-pink patches give the face an unsettled brightness; scribble lines sit on top of the structure rather than building it.","transitionFromPrevious":"W015's dense lines are packed and uniform; W021's scribble floats visibly above the face structure, loosening the mask into something more provisional."},{"slot":"W072","whyHere":"Magenta ground, mismatched eye forms — one gridded, one radial — and bared teeth hold confrontation and unease in the same flat space.","transitionFromPrevious":"W021's eyes are symmetrical flower bursts; W072's two eye zones refuse to match at all, fracturing the mask's symmetry."},{"slot":"W078","whyHere":"Wide flat-fronted head on a red ground, spiral eyes, and an open jaw with blocky teeth — the flattest and most frontal face in the chapter.","transitionFromPrevious":"W072's magenta field is cool; W078 returns to red, and the head fills the frame edge to edge, leaving almost no ground visible."}]},{"title":"Surface as Pressure","introduction":"Six faces where the marks covering the skin create a tension of their own — the tooth-filled mouth competes with a surface that seems to be doing something else entirely.","stops":[{"slot":"W009","whyHere":"Spiral-coil eyes and a rectangular open mouth read as shock, but layered color patches beneath the white outline fracture form and feeling simultaneously.","transitionFromPrevious":"W078's surface lines are loose and casual; W009's spiral eyes and dense color patches make the surface feel pressurised from within."},{"slot":"W024","whyHere":"Gold scribble fills the upper skull while solid black anchors the shoulders; bared teeth and green irises sit between warm chaos and cool weight.","transitionFromPrevious":"W009's pressure is distributed across the whole face; W024 splits the figure vertically — warm chaos above, solid black below — giving the tension a clear axis."},{"slot":"W030","whyHere":"White scribble lines pile across broad color patches, flattening depth even as the goggle eyes and bared teeth push toward alarm or exaggeration.","transitionFromPrevious":"W024's split is vertical; W030's white scribble covers the entire surface uniformly, dissolving the axis while keeping the same forward pressure."},{"slot":"W110","whyHere":"Dense overlapping lines pack the face until it reads as a container; identical flat eyes suggest a mask worn, while the tooth-filled mouth stays warm and loud.","transitionFromPrevious":"W030's scribble is white on color; W110's lines are multicolored and leave no gap, making the face feel more saturated and less readable as volume."},{"slot":"W064","whyHere":"Dense crosshatched strokes in lime, teal, red, and yellow pack every surface, yet thick black outlines hold the geometry firm; the stacked tooth bands read as both grin and grid.","transitionFromPrevious":"W110's outlines are loose green loops; W064's thick black geometry reasserts firm structure against the same dense interior line-work."},{"slot":"W130","whyHere":"Tooth-filled mouth and spiky gold brow forms pull against each other; dense black hatching builds weight at the core while cyan and pink lines escape outward.","transitionFromPrevious":"W064's lines are packed inside firm outlines; W130's lines escape beyond the head's boundary, suggesting pressure finding edges rather than being contained."}]},{"title":"Volume and Shadow","introduction":"Five faces that use modelled light and shadow rather than flat grounds, giving the teeth a different kind of weight — embedded in mass rather than announced against colour.","stops":[{"slot":"W027","whyHere":"Deep shadow on one side and a bleached highlight on the other build a solid mask-like volume; colored scribble sits across the modelled surface like static.","transitionFromPrevious":"W130's marks escape outward on a flat ground; W027 introduces genuine modelled volume, so the scribble lines read as surface noise on a solid form."},{"slot":"W087","whyHere":"Warm amber light rakes across a swollen face; one eye stares from a deep socket while the other sits empty, giving the blocky tooth row a grimace or cry quality.","transitionFromPrevious":"W027's volume is evenly modelled; W087's raking light and hollow socket introduce asymmetry and darkness that make the same tooth row feel more unsettled."},{"slot":"W112","whyHere":"Pink, lavender, gold, and deep red strokes build a rounded form against black; white teeth with canine-like protrusions pull the eye downward against a warm, murky upper mass.","transitionFromPrevious":"W087's face is lit from outside; W112's surface generates its own warmth from within, and the black ground replaces amber light with total darkness."},{"slot":"W050","whyHere":"A pale cap and broad moustache frame a close portrait; the fixed grin and clear eyes allow both a festive and an uneasy reading without resolving either.","transitionFromPrevious":"W112's form is abstract and lumpen; W050 introduces recognisable portrait features — cap, moustache, clear eyes — making the ambiguous grin feel more personally directed."},{"slot":"W053","whyHere":"A bulbous hat-wearing head floats on lime green; the compressed mouth and wide-set eyes read as wary, while jagged lines scatter across the swelling form like static.","transitionFromPrevious":"W050's portrait is close and direct; W053 pulls back to show a full head floating in open ground, replacing intimacy with a more guarded, held-back quality."}]},{"title":"The Expression That Will Not Settle","introduction":"Four faces where the open mouth and the surrounding marks pull in opposite directions, leaving the expression permanently unresolved.","stops":[{"slot":"W077","whyHere":"Hard angular eye shapes inside dense cross-hatched scribble create a visual standoff; the open mouth adds a second tension point without tipping into legible expression.","transitionFromPrevious":"W053's face is wary and compressed; W077's angular geometry inside soft scribble introduces a more active internal conflict between structure and surface."},{"slot":"W114","whyHere":"Lopsided eyes give an off-balance stare; the red-orange lip line is the only warm accent in a cool dark field, pulling the eye to the wide tooth-filled mouth.","transitionFromPrevious":"W077's conflict is between geometry and scribble; W114's conflict is between cool dark ground and the single warm red-orange lip line, making the mouth the only resolved point."},{"slot":"W120","whyHere":"A radiating collar of lobed forms gives the face ceremonial weight; spiral eyes pull inward while visible teeth and bright dots push energy back out simultaneously.","transitionFromPrevious":"W114's face is spare and cool; W120 is dense with ornament, so the same unresolved mouth now sits inside a structure that reads as both confrontational and festive."},{"slot":"W002","whyHere":"Radiating purple eyes locked wide open, diagonal light beams cutting across dense layered lines, and a rectangular tooth row below — alarm, grimace, and scream held at once.","transitionFromPrevious":"W120's ornament distributes energy outward; W002 compresses everything inward — the face fills the frame with no margin, making the unresolved expression feel inescapable."}]}]}
